notes: Magento storefront, direct HTTP fetch (no block, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow). English locale /ae-en/. Checked: homepage hero banner slider, homepage mid-page promo tiles, mega-menu, footer nav, sitemap2xl.xml, and site search (Amasty xsearch) for 'best seller'/'bestseller'/'clearance'/'outlet' etc - site search returns the same generic 'Furniture N items' filter block for every query term regardless of relevance, i.e. non-discriminating results, so it was not relied on as proof of anything, only as a supporting check. Also checked the Arabic locale (/ae-ar/) homepage hero slider - it links to the same URL slugs (ae-ar/most-loved, ae-ar/new-arrivals) reusing the same underlying Magento category ids as the English pages, so these are locale duplicates of the same listings, not additional rows. Found two genuine, distinct Bestsellers-type merchandising PLPs, both real Magento category listing pages with the site's own power-listing toolbar (count div + sort/filter UI, same mechanism verified reliable in the prior Furniture pass for this exact domain): (1) https://2xlhome.com/ae-en/bestsellers, h1 'Bestsellers', 127 items - linked twice from homepage promo tiles. (2) https://2xlhome.com/ae-en/most-loved, h1 'Most Loved', 134 items - linked from the homepage hero slider (slide background image filename is literally best_seller_banner.jpg, reused from an earlier 'best sellers' banner asset). Different item counts and different product-id sets on the two pages confirm they are genuinely different listings, not aliases of one page. 'Most Loved' is not one of the brief's exact target phrases, but functions as a popularity/customer-favorites merchandising concept (a real distinct PLP, own toolbar, own curated product set, positioned next to the literal Bestsellers page in the site's own promo layout) so it is recorded here with a terminology flag for reviewer judgment rather than silently dropped or silently merged.
